help.discard.saferChoice: Not sure? Cancel and choose Take a snapshot first. It only costs disk space.
help.discard.saferChoiceKeep: Not sure? Cancel and keep them as a new profile first. It only costs disk space.
help.newChanges.answer: Files in this folder changed since the last snapshot, from saving in the game, a mod manager, or a game update. Take a snapshot to keep them, or discard them to put the folder back as the snapshot has it.
help.newChanges.question: What are new changes?
help.olderChoice.answer: Pick Keep this session as a new profile if you might want the newer snapshots of "{profileName}" again. It stays as it is. Pick Continue only if you're done with them. They move to Recently removed, and you can bring them back as a new profile until you next free up space.
help.olderChoice.question: Which should I pick?
help.page.activity.body: Activity lists what SavePoint is doing and has done for a game: taking snapshots, switching files, starting the game, freeing up space. Details shows each step of a job, which you can copy into a bug report. Cancel stops a job that can be stopped.
help.page.activity.title: Activity
help.page.afterPlay.body: When you close the game, SavePoint asks what to do with the session. Keep it as a new snapshot (the safe choice), replace the latest snapshot with it, or choose Not now and SavePoint asks again before your next switch.
help.page.afterPlay.title: After you play
help.page.basics.body: A game is the folder it is installed in, plus the folder its saves live in. A profile is one way of playing it, such as Vanilla or Modded 1.6, with its own game version, mods and saves. A snapshot is a copy of a profile as it was at one moment. SavePoint takes one when you create a profile and each time you keep a session.
help.page.basics.title: Games, profiles and snapshots
help.page.intro: SavePoint keeps the game setups that work, so you can go back to them. These ideas come in the order you meet them.
help.page.newChanges.body: New changes are files in your game folders that changed since the last snapshot, such as a new save or a mod your mod manager added. SavePoint won't switch over them. Take a snapshot to keep them in their profile, or discard them to restore the last snapshot's files.
help.page.newChanges.title: New changes
help.page.older.body: When you play from an older snapshot, your session can't go on the end of the profile. Keep this session as a new profile, and the original stays as it is, newer snapshots included. Or continue the profile from your session, and its newer snapshots go to Recently removed.
help.page.older.title: Going back to an older snapshot
help.page.permanent.body: SavePoint can't take any of these back.
help.page.permanent.delete: Deleting a profile, which deletes the snapshots only it holds, or deleting a game, which deletes all of its snapshots.
help.page.permanent.emptyFolder: Starting with an empty snapshot folder when SavePoint can't reach the old one.
help.page.permanent.freeUp: Freeing up space, which deletes what is in Recently removed for good.
help.page.permanent.noteClosing: SavePoint asks a second time before each of these. It never sends your files anywhere. Its only network request is for game artwork, which you can turn off in Settings.
help.page.permanent.noteRecoverable: Replacing a snapshot and continuing a profile can be undone. What they remove waits in Recently removed until you next free up space.
help.page.permanent.title: What can't be undone
help.page.play.body: Play makes your game folders match the profile, then starts the game. If anything would change, SavePoint shows what first, and nothing changes until you press Switch and play. To put the files in place without starting the game, for example to work on mods, choose Switch to this profile from the profile's menu. SavePoint then doesn't ask what to do with a session afterwards.
help.page.play.title: What Play does
help.page.removed.body: Replacing a snapshot, or continuing a profile from an older one, takes snapshots off a profile. They wait in History under Recently removed, and you can bring any back as a new profile until you next free up space.
help.page.removed.title: Recently removed
help.page.saves.body: A save is the game's own file, made when you save in the game. A save snapshot holds your whole saves folder as it was at one moment. Going back to one puts those files in place, and you still load the save you want inside the game.
help.page.saves.title: Saves and snapshots are different
help.page.space.body: SavePoint keeps snapshots in one folder, which you can see and move in Settings. A game's first snapshot is the big one, and later ones only add what changed. Free up space clears out snapshots no profile uses, such as a deleted profile's, and the ones in Recently removed.
help.page.space.title: The snapshot folder and freeing up space
help.page.title: How SavePoint works
help.picture.basics.legend: Each dot is a snapshot. The newest is on the right.
help.picture.removed.bringBack: Bring back as a new profile
help.replace.answer: Only when you won't want "{snapshotName}" as it was. What it held goes to Recently removed, and you can bring it back as a new profile until you next free up space. Keeping a new snapshot is always safe. It only uses disk space.
help.replace.question: When should I replace?
help.row.loaded: This profile's files are in your game folders right now.
help.row.newChanges: Files in your game folders changed since this profile's last snapshot.
help.saveSnapshot.answer: Each choice is your whole saves folder as it was at one moment. SavePoint puts those files in place, and you still pick the save to load inside the game.
help.saveSnapshot.question: What's a save snapshot?
help.snapshot.answer: A snapshot is a copy SavePoint keeps of a profile's game version, mods and saves (or just some of them) at one moment. SavePoint takes one when you create a profile and each time you keep a session. Choose Go back to this on a snapshot to play from that moment, or Switch to this snapshot to load it without playing.
help.snapshot.question: What's a snapshot?
help.space.answer: A game's first snapshot can take about as much space as the game itself, and the new-profile check shows the exact amount. Later snapshots only add files that changed, so they're usually small.
help.space.question: How much space do snapshots take?
help.tour.findAgain: You can see this again in Settings > Help.
help.tour.history.body: History lists every snapshot. Choose Go back to this on one to play from that moment, even after the game updates, or Switch to this snapshot to load it without starting the game.
help.tour.history.title: Go back any time
help.tour.newProfile.body: Want a different mod list or game version? Make another profile. Each keeps its own snapshots, and Play switches between them.
help.tour.newProfile.title: Try something new safely
help.tour.play.body: Play makes your game folders match this profile, then starts the game. When you close it, SavePoint asks whether to keep the session as a new snapshot. To load the files without starting the game, choose Switch to this profile from the profile's menu.
help.tour.play.title: Play puts the right files in place
help.tour.profile.body: A profile is one way of playing {gameName}, with its own game version, mods and saves. Its snapshots are copies of all three at one moment.
help.tour.profile.title: This is a profile
settings.help.heading: Help
settings.help.hint: The few ideas SavePoint uses, in plain words.
settings.help.tourNeedsProfile: The tour needs a game that has a profile to show.
